blocks.title: Protect the object invariant
blocks.text: The constructor refuses a negative opening balance before storing it. The field is private, so outside code must use approved public methods instead of bypassing validation.

blocks.title: Worked example · Construct a valid account; control updates
blocks.text: using System; Account savings = new Account(10); savings.Deposit(5); Console.WriteLine(savings.GetBalance()); class Account { private int balance; public Account(int opening) { if (opening < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(); balance = opening; } public int GetBalance()…

blocks.title: Worked example · Constructor sets the initial state
blocks.text: new Account(10) invokes Account(int opening) . It checks 10 is non-negative, then stores 10 in the private field balance .

blocks.title: Worked example · Method validates the proposed change
blocks.text: savings.Deposit(5) passes the positive-amount check and increases balance from 10 to 15. Outside code cannot change the private field directly.

blocks.title: Trace a different validated account
blocks.text: Using the Account class, run Account current = new Account(20); current.Deposit(7); Then attempt current.Deposit(-2); . What does current.GetBalance() give afterwards if the exception is caught by the caller?

blocks.text: What happens at construction, after the valid deposit, and at the attempted negative deposit?

blocks.title: 27; invalid deposit rejected
blocks.text: Constructor sets 20; valid deposit makes 27. The second call raises an ArgumentOutOfRangeException before the assignment; when the caller handles it, the balance remains 27 .

MODEL ANSWER Reject invalid initial state if (w <= 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(w)); width = w; goes inside public Box(int w) . Width 4 is accepted; width 0 is rejected.
